answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. The inlet decay curve is applied at each close, dawn records the drop, and gale recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 4 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. That bill is paid per identity, so 384 aliases cost 128 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
